title: Cofibrant simplicial inversion is base change of total groupoid completion
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the Bergner structure, object-preserving replacement $R$ and $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Fix a small set $O$ of objects and let $i:A\to B$ be a cofibration between cofibrant simplicial categories with object set $O$, identity on objects. Let $G(A)=A[A^{-1}]$ be obtained by groupoid-completing the ordinary category in each simplicial degree. Let $B[A^{-1}]$ denote degreewise inversion of the images of arrows of $A$. The ordinary pushout square of simplicial categories
$$\begin{array}{ccc} A&\longrightarrow&G(A)\\ \downarrow i&&\downarrow\\ B&\longrightarrow&B[A^{-1}]\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pushout for the Bergner homotopy theory. Equivalently, replacing the span by a cofibrant span and taking its pushout gives a Dwyer--Kan equivalence to this displayed pushout. The simplicial map
$$\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)\longrightarrow\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}(G(A))$$
induced by total inversion is a weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets and its target is a Kan complex. These assertions are natural in maps of the cofibrant pairs. They impose no requirement that the image of $A$ be saturated or satisfy two-out-of-three in $B$.

source.place: Sections 7.2-7.6 (fixed-object model structure and cofibrations), 8.1-8.2 (homotopy meaning of pushout), 9.1-9.2 (cofibrant groupoid completion), 10.1 and 10.3 (cofibrant localization), printed pp.276-281. The Bergner/coherent-nerve formulation is the derived-inversion formulation in Hinich Section 1.2, printed pp.5-6, especially its paragraph citing DK1 9.2 and its cocartesian diagram (5). This is the unsaturated cofibrant-pair version; the subsequent saturated-marking Proposition 1.2.1 is not used as a black box. No Stacks tag states these enriched assertions.

proof.text: Write $C=G(A)$ and let $j:A\to C$ be total inversion. For any simplicial category $T$, a functor $B\to T$ extends across degreewise inversion exactly when it carries every degreewise arrow in the image of $A$ to an invertible arrow in the corresponding ordinary category $T_n$. In that case its restriction to $A$ extends uniquely to $C$, by sending each formal inverse to the inverse of its image. These extensions commute with all simplicial operators, since functors preserve inverses uniquely. Thus the displayed square is the ordinary pushout, computed in fixed-object simplicial categories and also in all simplicial categories. This universal-property argument also applies to targets whose object set differs from $O$: both legs specify the same object function.

source.place: Section 3.1 ordinary inversion universal property and Section 9.1 degreewise completion; direct word argument

proof.text: Put $C=G(A)$. By [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus], factor $A\to C$ functorially in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ as a cofibration $j:A\hookrightarrow\widetilde C$ followed by a trivial fibration $p:\widetilde C\to C$. The same node identifies the given Bergner cofibration $i:A\to B$ and the cofibrancy of $A,B$ with their fixed-object counterparts, and identifies $j$ with a Bergner cofibration. For the direct Reedy category with objects $a,b,c$ and nonidentity arrows $a\to b,a\to c$, choose degrees $0,1,1$. In the span $B\leftarrow A\to\widetilde C$, the latching objects are the initial object at $a$ and $A$ at both $b,c$. Thus [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] makes this a cofibrant span in the Bergner structure: its three latching maps are the initial map of $A$, $i$, and $j$. The map to the original span is the identity on $A,B$ and $p$ on its third object. It is objectwise a Dwyer--Kan equivalence since $p$ fixes objects and is a weak equivalence on every mapping set. Hence this is a cofibrant replacement span of the kind stipulated in the statement. Write $\widetilde P=B\amalg_A\widetilde C$ for its pushout.

source.place: Sections 7.2 and 8.1; functorial factorization and the direct Reedy span criterion

proof.text: The map $k:\widetilde C\to\widetilde P$ is a fixed-object cofibration. Indeed, a lifting square against $k$ and a trivial fibration restricts, along $A\to\widetilde C$ and $B\to\widetilde P$, to a lifting square against $i$. A lift for $i$ and the given map from $\widetilde C$ agree on $A$, so the pushout universal property combines them into the required lift against $k$. Apply [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-left-proper] to the weak equivalence $p:\widetilde C\to C$ and cofibration $k$. It gives a local weak equivalence $\widetilde P\to C\amalg_{\widetilde C}\widetilde P$. Cocones for the latter object are pairs of maps from $C,B$ agreeing on $A$, so it is canonically $C\amalg_A B=B[A^{-1}]$ by step 1. The comparison fixes $O$ and induces bijections on components of every mapping set. Its $\pi_0$ functor is therefore fully faithful and surjective on objects, hence an equivalence. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] this local weak equivalence is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Consequently the displayed ordinary pushout is the required Bergner homotopy pushout.

source.place: Proposition 7.3(ii), proved in Section 8.3; cofibration cobase change checked by lifting

proof.text: Let $D(V)=\operatorname{diag}_{p,q}N_p(V_q)$. Cofibrancy of $A$ and [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus] give a retract $A\to E\to A$ with $E_q$ free for every $q$. Apply degreewise groupoid completion and ordinary nerve to this retraction. For every $q$, the canonical $N(E_q)\to N(G(E_q))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-free-category-groupoid-nerve]. Consequently $N(A_q)\to N(G(A_q))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, as a retract of that map. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence], now to the degreewise ordinary nerves, to conclude that $D(A)\to D(G(A))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 9.2 proof from Proposition 7.6 and Proposition 3.7, pp.272,278-279

proof.text: For $V=A$ and $V=G(A)$ use the natural weak homotopy equivalence $z_V:D(V)\to D(RV)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RV)$ in [lem-coef-diagonal-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The comparison theorem is applied only to the locally Kan objects $RV$. Naturality gives the commutative square with upper edge $D(A)\to D(G(A))$, lower edge $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RA)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RG(A))$, and vertical edges $z_A,z_{G(A)}$. All but the lower edge are weak homotopy equivalences by step 4 and the cited comparison. Two-out-of-three proves that the lower edge is a weak homotopy equivalence. By the specified definition of $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}$, this is precisely the map in the statement, rather than an unrelated equivalence of homotopy types.

source.place: Definition 1.7, Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 4.3, printed pp.31,33-34,40, applied after locally Kan replacement

proof.text: The ordinary category $G(A)_0$ is a groupoid. Every arrow representing a morphism of $\pi_0G(A)$ is represented by a vertex of a mapping set; its inverse in $G(A)_0$ represents an inverse of its component. Thus $\pi_0G(A)$ is a groupoid. The object-preserving local weak equivalence $G(A)\to RG(A)$ induces bijections on all such component sets, respecting composition and identities, so $\pi_0RG(A)$ is also a groupoid. It is locally Kan by construction. The last clause of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] now gives that $N_{\mathrm{hc}}RG(A)$ is Kan, as required.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.5.1 and the locally Kan coherent-nerve criterion of the cited node

proof.text: Total inversion is functorial: a functor sends a formal inverse of an arrow to the inverse of its image, and uniqueness preserves compositions and identities. The pushout identification in step 1 commutes with this formula and therefore with maps of the pairs. The factorization used in step 2 can be functorial by [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus]; pushout comparisons are then natural by their universal properties. The retractions in step 4 only verify weak equivalences and do not define any claimed map. Finally $R$ is functorial by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and the maps $z_V$ and their squares are natural by [lem-coef-diagonal-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Thus the total-inversion map and the homotopy-pushout comparison have the asserted naturality. The argument used no saturation or two-out-of-three hypothesis on the image of $A$ in $B$.

source.place: Sections 3.1-3.3, 9.1 and 10.1; functorial inverse words and pushout comparisons
